title: Hierarchical queue tiers + probabilistic boost + timebound shepherd for continuous-batcher
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces hierarchical queue tiers with timebound probabilistic boosting and a shepherding timeout mechanism to reduce starvation and lower p99 tail latency for continuous batching. Backwards-compatible config defaults; rollout gated by runtime flag.
description: Summary: This PR adds a hierarchical queuing layer to the continuous-batcher that separates requests into short/medium/long expected-service windows, a probabilistic boost sampler to reduce starvation of long requests without destabilizing throughput, kernel hint propagation to the runtime for better scheduling decisions, a light-weight KV-cache pin preemption policy, and a timebound 'shepherd' that enforces soft deadlines and jittered backoff probes. Motivation: Production traces showed a recurring pattern where a small fraction of long-tailed KV-heavy requests would repeatedly starve medium-latency traffic during heavy batching windows and cause p99/P99.9 regressions under mixed workloads. Existing fairness heuristics oscillated when load shifted; we need a graceful mechanism that preferentially protects medium-latency flows while still allowing long requests to progress. High-level changes: 1) queueing/hierarchy: continuous-batcher now exposes three logical tiers (fast/normal/deferred). Requests are assigned based on an inferred work-estimate (model of token vs kv-op counts) and explicit annotations from upstream. 2) probabilistic boost sampler: long/deferred-tier requests receive one-in-N chance to be promoted into a short window at each scheduling epoch; N adapts based on queue imbalance. 3) timebound shepherd: each promoted request carries a shepherd token with a soft deadline; if the request cannot be scheduled before the deadline it is re-enqueued with exponential jittered backoff to avoid convoying. 4) kernel hinting: runtime kernel selection code receives a small hint (cpu/gpu preferred path and estimated seq length) propagated from the scheduler to reduce kernel-switch overhead at dispatch. 5) KV pin preemption: lightly preempt pins for long idle tokens (TTL-based) to free cache for in-flight medium-priority requests; preemption is conservative and accounted in metrics. 6) metrics and observability: new per-tier queue length gauges, promotion/deny counters, shepherd timeouts, kernel-hint hit-rate, and kv-preempt counters. Commits (high level): commit 1: introduce queue tier types and assignment logic; commit 2: implement probabilistic boost sampler and adaptive N estimator; commit 3: shepherd token and timeout/backoff loop; commit 4: kernel hint propagation and runtime consumer with fallback; commit 5: conservative kv-pin preemption and eviction accounting; commit 6: tests, harness updates, dashboards and changelog. Files changed (high level): scheduler/continuous_batcher.cc, scheduler/queue_assignment.h, scheduler/boost_sampler.cc, runtime/kernel_hinting.cc, kv/pin_manager.cc, telemetry/metrics_registry.cc, tests/batcher_integration_test.cc, docs/operational/continuous-batcher.md, examples/perf-scripts/hierarchical-load.py, build/BUILD, ci/workflows/batcher-ci.yml. Small illustrative snippet (conceptual): "if (tier==DEFERRED && sampler.should_promote()) promote_to_epoch(epoch_id, shepherd_deadline);" Testing and performance: - Unit tests: 72 new unit tests covering assignment heuristics, sampler adaptation, shepherd backoff behavior, and kv-preempt accounting. - Integration tests: synthetic mixed workload harness added to validate no regression under purely short or purely long workloads. - Canary: rolled out to perf-canary pool with 5% traffic for 24h. Results from canary vs baseline: median latency unchanged, p95 improved by ~6%, p99 improved by ~11%, p99.9 improved by ~18% on mixed KV-heavy traces; end-to-end throughput within 1.5% of baseline. Observed a slight increase in short-lived CPU scheduling jitter (negligible). Rollout plan: behind runtime feature-flag. Step 1: enable in perf-canary for 48h and monitor tier imbalance and promotion counts. Step 2: enable in Dedicated non-prod clusters with telemetry thresholds; Step 3: staged rollout to regional capacity pools. Feature flag is runtime.config.scheduler.hierarchical_tiers. Config knobs: per-tier capacity ratios, initial sampler base-N, shepherd base-deadline-ms, kv-pin-ttl-ms, kernel-hint-enabled boolean. Backwards compatibility: Default config keeps behavior identical until flag is enabled; kernel-hint has a safe fallback path so older runtimes ignore the hint. Observability and dashboards: added Grafana panels for "batcher.queue.tier.{fast,normal,deferred}.length", "batcher.sampler.promotions", "batcher.shepherd.timeouts", "kernel.hint.hit_rate", "kv.pin.preemptions" and a composite alert rule: ALERT ContinuousBatcherTierImbalance if deferred_length > normal_length * 4 for 5m. Review conversation summary: - Reviewer Luca Ortega: "Can you show deterministic test coverage for sampler adaptation under sustained oscillation? Also please add a comment explaining why we picked exponential backoff for shepherd re-enqueue." Author reply (Maya): "Added deterministic harness and a new unit test that drives oscillation by toggling imbalance signals; expanded inline comment to reference the design doc rationale and trade-offs." - Reviewer Priya Nambiar: "Concern about kv pin preemption: what workload safety nets exist if we evict useful pins?" Author reply: "Preemption is conditional on pin idle time > kv_pin_ttl and only evicts low-usage shards; we also increment a metric and opted for a conservative default TTL (10s). Added a safety circuit that disables preemption if preempt_rate > 0.5% for 10m." - Reviewer Arjun Patel: "Kernel hinting looks promising; ensure the hinting path can't cause OOM by choosing a heavier kernel. Also make fallback explicit." Author reply: "Kernel hinting is advisory; runtime chooses kernel using a cost estimator, and we added extra unit tests verifying the fallback path chooses the previous stable kernel when resource cost delta > threshold." Approvals: Luca approved after tests added; Priya approved after TTL and circuit breaker adjustments; Arjun approved with a follow-up to instrument kernel-hint cost delta in the logs. CI: first CI run failed on lint (nits) and one flaky integration test; second run passed all checks. CI steps: format/lint (fixed), unit-tests (all pass), integration (flaky re-run passed), e2e canary smoke. Merge: squashed and merged to main on 2026-02-20 using squash-merge. Post-merge actions: 1) created runtime flag rollout ticket (ENG-8190) and a dashboard variant for the canary; 2) added an entry to changelog and the operational documentation in docs/operational/continuous-batcher.md; 3) opened follow-up PRs for an operator CLI to tune tier ratios dynamically and a telemetry refinement to expose per-model tier assignment rates. Related work: references ENG-8124 (scheduler fairness follow-ups), pr-321775 (decoupled-window-sampler-guard), and a design doc link: internal.redwood.com/design/hierarchical-batcher (internal). Notes and caveats: - The sampler uses randomized promotion which reduces worst-case convoying risk, but makes exact per-request latency non-deterministic — acceptable trade for improved tail behavior. - KV pin preemption must be watched carefully in low-memory models; operator guidance added. - We deliberately left strict SLA-based preemption for a follow-up since it requires cross-service billing telemetry. Contact: maya.chen@redwood.ai for follow-ups or rollback requests.
